title: Local drummers and the Liberty Theater band
summary: He names early New Orleans theater drummers, the Liberty Theater band, and trapping rats in the organ, which let him sight-read at the Sanger.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Which drummers in this town do you remember the most strong?
Well, the only ones that I can remember...
I'm talking about when you were growing up and learning to play drums in town.

It was Paul Detrite. Paul Detrite. He was at the Orphium Theater. Uh-huh. Then Gosley. Adrian Gosley. He was always at one of the shows. Uh-huh. But Jimmy Boyle was not a good drummer. He was at the Liberty Theater. He was not a great drummer. He was a very handsome guy. He looked like Adolf Nenju. And he wore, always wore a white suit. Except at one time he was at the Liberty Theater when a rat got caught in one of the fans up there. The rat got torn to pieces and there was blood all over his white suit. Oh! Well, they had fans, big fans at their... Exhaust fans.
I mean, fans maybe six or seven feet in diameter. And that was one thing. But they had a good band at the Liberty. They had Witt Lebowski. You heard of Witt Lebowski?
I've heard him on records, huh?

Witt Lebowski. He had a brother who was a violinist. But Witt Lebowski had a way that he could break a string on a piano. Very easily. If he was mad at you, he'd close the piano down and put his feet up on the piano like this and wouldn't touch it. They had Tony Papalia was with him down there. Jimmy Boyle. Johnny Karugi was on fiddle. And the funny thing about it, Robert Morton and Ray McNamara were the organist. And I used to stay down there at night to close, to put, I don't know if I told you, to put the trap on the organ?
For the rats. Do you know about that?
Yeah, you told me about that.

You told me about that. That's how I got to know Ray and Bob Morton very well. And the funny thing about it, and maybe I'm repeating myself, but when I went to the Sanger Theater, they were surprised that I read so well. You know why? Same show. It was the same music they were playing at the Liberty Theater. I knew it by heart. They were very surprised that I read so well.
